writeup: TIC 411978234 is an eclipsing binary candidate with an orbital period of 8.5622 days. Observations from TESS show the primary star dims by 2.98% during eclipse, with a secondary eclipse detected at 9.6 sigma significance occurring at orbital phase 0.48. The binary light-curve signal reaches a detection significance of 132.8 on the Box Least Squares scale. Pixel-level analysis using difference imaging confirms the signal near the target location, though the centroid offset of 3.3 arcseconds warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it potentially novel. The automated ML screening assigned it a score of 0.74, indicating reasonable confidence that this represents a genuine eclipsing binary system rather than an instrumental artifact or false positive.
